stimuli.text: Initial-rate data for A + B → products:
A student heats 11.2 g of $$\ce{CaCO3(s)}$$, which decomposes completely: $$\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$$. The $$\ce{CO2}$$ is collected at 304 K and 1.05 atm.
The decomposition of compound X was monitored at constant temperature.
A student titrates 23.0 mL of 0.12 M weak monoprotic acid HA (Ka = 3 \times 10^{-5}) with 0.1 M NaOH.
7.8 g of $$\ce{NH4NO3}$$ dissolves in 101 g of water in a coffee-cup calorimeter. The temperature falls by 7.7 °C. Assume the solution's specific heat is 4.18 J/(g·°C).

A galvanic cell is made of a Zn electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Zn^{2+}}$$ and a Pb electrode in 1.0 M $$\ce{Pb^{2+}}$$. Standard reduction potentials: $$\ce{Zn^{2+} + 2e- -> Zn}$$ E° = -0.76 V; $$\ce{Pb^{2+} + 2e- -> Pb}$$ E° = -0.13 V.
The photoelectron spectra of Mg (Z = 12) and Al (Z = 13) are compared.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.01 M solution of $$\ce{NaOH}$$ at 25 °C?

options.why: Correct. Strong base: [OH⁻] = 1 × 0.01 M; pH = 14 − pOH.
That is the pOH; subtract from 14.
Strong acids and bases ionize completely; no equilibrium is needed.

questions.stem: A solution has an absorbance of 0.671 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 839 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
How can an unfavorable reaction (ΔG positive) be made to occur?

options.text: By coupling it to a favorable reaction so the total ΔG is negative

questions.stem: Which compound has the greater lattice energy, $$\ce{NaF}$$ or $$\ce{MgO}$$?

options.text: $$\ce{NaF}$$, because its ions have larger charges
$$\ce{MgO}$$, because its ions have larger charges
options.why: Correct. By Coulomb's law, attraction increases with the product of the ion charges.

options.text: $$\ce{NaF}$$, because it has more atoms per formula unit
options.why: Number of atoms does not determine lattice energy.

options.text: They are equal because both are ionic

questions.explanation: MgO has ion charges 2 and 2; NaF has 1 and 1.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 45 min. Starting at 16.7 M, what is the concentration after 135 min?

options.why: Each half-life halves the concentration; it is not divided by 2n.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.7 mol N₂, 0.2 mol O₂ and 0.3 mol Ar at a total pressure of 3.3 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: The gases are not present in equal amounts.
Use the mole fraction, not moles.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.1 M solution of $$\ce{KOH}$$ at 25 °C?

options.why: Strong acids and bases ionize completely; no equilibrium is needed.
That is the pOH; subtract from 14.
Correct. Strong base: [OH⁻] = 1 × 0.1 M; pH = 14 − pOH.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.3 mol N₂, 0.4 mol O₂ and 0.7 mol Ar at a total pressure of 5 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: Use the mole fraction, not moles.
The gases are not present in equal amounts.

questions.stem: Why is the radius of F⁻ larger than that of F?

options.text: F⁻ has an additional electron shell
The added electron increases electron–electron repulsion with the same nuclear charge
options.why: Correct. Anions are larger than their atoms.

questions.explanation: Anions are larger than their atoms.

questions.stem: A gas mixture contains 0.8 mol N₂, 0.9 mol O₂ and 0.3 mol Ar at a total pressure of 2.6 atm. What is the partial pressure of N₂?

options.why: Use the mole fraction, not moles.
The gases are not present in equal amounts.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of N in $$\ce{NH3}$$?

options.why: Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Make the oxidation numbers add up to the overall charge.
Correct. The oxidation numbers must sum to the species' overall charge (O usually −2, H usually +1).

questions.stem: How many formula units or molecules are in 176 g of $$\ce{C3H8}$$?

options.why: Correct. Convert grams to moles, then multiply by Avogadro's number.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 8.6. In a solution at pH 6.6, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Below the pKa, the protonated form dominates.

questions.stem: A 23.1 mL sample of $$\ce{H2SO4}$$ is titrated to the equivalence point with 24.4 mL of 0.292 M NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

questions.stem: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 9.1 g. The actual yield is 8.4 g. What is the percent yield?
For $$\ce{2N2O5 -> 4NO2 + O2}$$, $$\ce{N2O5}$$ is consumed at 0.71 M/s. At what rate does $$\ce{NO2}$$ form?

options.why: Divide by the reactant's coefficient too.
Correct. Multiply by the coefficient ratio 4/2.

questions.stem: In paper chromatography with a nonpolar solvent, which component travels farthest?

options.why: Correct. It is most attracted to the nonpolar mobile phase.
Polar components stay with the polar paper.

questions.explanation: It is most attracted to the nonpolar mobile phase.

questions.stem: Which bond is the most polar?

options.why: Correct. It has the largest electronegativity difference (1.2).

questions.stem: A reaction has K = 45. What is K for the reaction multiplied by ½?

options.why: Multiplying by n raises K to the nth power.
K is raised to a power, not multiplied.
Correct. Reverse → 1/K; multiply by n → Kⁿ.

questions.stem: If ΔH = −286 kJ for H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O(l), what is ΔH for 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂ + O₂?
For $$\ce{A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g)}$$, K = 3.6. A mixture has [A] = 0.8 M, [B] = 0.4 M and [C] = 0.8 M. In which direction will the reaction proceed?

options.text: It is at equilibrium, because Q = K
It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 2.5
It proceeds in reverse, toward reactants, because Q = 2
options.why: If Q is less than K, the reaction proceeds forward.

options.text: It proceeds forward, toward products, because Q = 2
options.why: Correct. Q = [C]²/([A][B]) = 2, which is less than K.

questions.stem: In HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺, which species is the Brønsted–Lowry base?
The nitrate ion has three resonance structures. What is true of its N–O bonds?

options.text: One is double and two are single at all times
They alternate rapidly between single and double
All three are identical, intermediate between single and double bonds

questions.stem: What is the energy of a photon with a wavelength of 281 nm?

options.why: Correct. E = hc/λ, with λ in meters.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$, initial [H₂] = 1.7 M and [I₂] = 1.5 M, with no HI. At equilibrium, [HI] = 1.14 M. What is K?
Samples of $$\ce{He}$$, $$\ce{Ar}$$, $$\ce{N2}$$, $$\ce{O2}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.
O2 has a larger molar mass (32 g/mol).
N2 has a larger molar mass (28 g/mol).
Ar has a larger molar mass (40 g/mol).

questions.explanation: Molar masses: He 4, Ar 40, N2 28, O2 32.

questions.stem: Is $$\ce{PCl3}$$ polar or nonpolar, and why?

options.text: Polar, because its bond dipoles do not cancel
Nonpolar, because it has no polar bonds
options.why: Polarity depends on both bond polarity and geometry.

options.text: Nonpolar, because its bond dipoles cancel by symmetry
options.why: Consider the molecule's shape, not only its bonds.
Containing H does not make a molecule polar.

questions.explanation: PCl3 is trigonal pyramidal; the dipoles do not cancel.

questions.stem: Which indicator is best for titrating acetic acid with NaOH (equivalence pH ≈ 8.7)?

options.why: Correct. Its range includes the equivalence pH.

questions.explanation: Its range includes the equivalence pH.

questions.stem: What is the pressure of 2.44 mol of gas in a 20 L container at 324 K?

options.why: With L and atm, use R = 0.08206.

questions.stem: 43 g of water at 75 °C is mixed with 195 g of water at 27 °C in an insulated container. What is the final temperature?

options.why: Pair each mass with its own temperature.
Correct. Heat lost = heat gained; for water alone, a mass-weighted average.

questions.stem: What is E°cell for a galvanic cell made from these half-cells?

options.why: E° does not change when half-reactions are multiplied.
Cathode minus anode; a galvanic cell is positive.

questions.stem: Calculate ΔH° for $$\ce{C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O(l)}$$. (ΔH°f of O₂ is 0.)

options.why: Correct. Σ n ΔH°f(products) − Σ n ΔH°f(reactants).
Multiply each ΔH°f by its coefficient.

questions.stem: When a reaction involving 0.076 mol of limiting reactant occurs in 143 g of solution (c = 4.18 J/(g·°C)), the temperature rises by 10.1 °C. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Divide by the moles of reactant.
A temperature rise means the reaction is exothermic (negative ΔH).
Correct. q(solution) = mcΔT = 6040 J; q(reaction) = −q(solution); divide by moles.

questions.stem: A solution has an absorbance of 0.594 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 99 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 22 kJ/mol, the transition state at 93 kJ/mol and the products at 55 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy of the reverse reaction?

options.why: Measure from the correct starting point.
Correct. Reverse Ea = transition state − products.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 71, ΔH = 33, reverse Ea = 38 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: In a mechanism, a species that is produced in one step and consumed in a later step is a(n):

options.why: A catalyst is consumed first and regenerated later.
Correct. It does not appear in the overall equation.

questions.explanation: It does not appear in the overall equation.

questions.stem: Samples of $$\ce{O2}$$, $$\ce{Ar}$$, $$\ce{N2}$$, $$\ce{H2}$$ are all at the same temperature. Which has the highest average molecular speed?

options.why: Correct. At the same temperature, average kinetic energy is equal, so the lightest gas moves fastest.
O2 has a larger molar mass (32 g/mol).
Ar has a larger molar mass (40 g/mol).
N2 has a larger molar mass (28 g/mol).

questions.explanation: Molar masses: O2 32, Ar 40, N2 28, H2 2.02.

questions.stem: A 11.9 mL sample of $$\ce{H2SO4}$$ is titrated to the equivalence point with 39.3 mL of 0.061 M NaOH. What is the concentration of the acid?

options.why: Correct. Each H₂SO₄ reacts with two OH⁻, so divide the moles of NaOH by 2.

questions.stem: 55 mL of 12 M solution is diluted to 217 mL. What is the new concentration?

options.why: V₂ is the total final volume.

questions.stem: The first four ionization energies of an element are 625, 1150, 2024, 16192 kJ/mol. In which group of the periodic table is the element most likely found?

options.why: Correct. The large jump comes after removing 3 electrons, so it has 3 valence electrons.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.
Locate the largest jump between successive ionization energies.

questions.explanation: The big jump marks the start of removing core electrons.

questions.stem: A weak acid HA has pKa = 9.4. In a solution at pH 7.3, which statement is correct?

options.why: Correct. Below the pKa, the protonated form dominates.

questions.stem: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH negative, which change shifts the equilibrium toward NH₃?

options.why: The reaction is exothermic; heating shifts left.
Correct. The product side has fewer moles of gas.

questions.explanation: The product side has fewer moles of gas.

questions.stem: What is the mass percent of O in $$\ce{CO2}$$?

options.why: There are 2 atoms of O in the formula.
Use masses, not numbers of atoms.
That is the percent of the other elements.

questions.stem: On a reaction energy profile, the reactants are at 74 kJ/mol, the transition state at 213 kJ/mol and the products at 158 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.why: Measure from the correct starting point.

questions.explanation: Forward Ea = 139, ΔH = 84, reverse Ea = 55 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: How many valence electrons are shown in the Lewis structure of $$\ce{CO3^{2-}}$$?

options.why: Correct. Sum the valence electrons of all atoms, then add one per negative charge (subtract one per positive charge).

questions.stem: A solution has an absorbance of 0.772 in a 2 cm cuvette. The molar absorptivity is 429 M⁻¹cm⁻¹. What is the concentration?
Reaction 1 has ΔH₁ = -102 kJ and reaction 2 has ΔH₂ = 64 kJ. A target reaction is obtained by doubling reaction 1 and adding reaction 2. What is ΔH for the target reaction?

options.why: Reversing changes the sign of ΔH₂.
Correct. Reverse → change sign; multiply → multiply ΔH; then add.
Enthalpies add; they do not multiply.

questions.stem: Use the bond enthalpies to estimate ΔH for $$\ce{H2 + F2 -> 2HF}$$.

options.why: Correct. ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).
Broken minus formed, not formed minus broken.
Multiply each bond energy by the number of bonds.
Bonds formed release energy: subtract them.

questions.stem: A buffer contains 0.36 mol of a weak acid HA (pKa 9.25) and 0.08 mol of A⁻. What is its pH?
A weak acid (pKa 4.74) is titrated with NaOH; the equivalence point is reached at 92.3 mL. What is the pH after 46.1 mL of NaOH has been added?

options.why: Correct. At the half-equivalence point, [HA] = [A⁻], so pH = pKa.
That is only for strong acid–strong base equivalence.

questions.stem: The Ksp of $$\ce{AgBr}$$ is 5 \times 10^{-13}. What is its molar solubility in a solution that already contains 0.05 M of its anion?

options.why: That is the solubility in pure water.
The common ion's concentration dominates; no square root.
Correct. Ksp = s(c), so s = Ksp/c.

questions.stem: A compound (glucose) is 40% C, 6.71% H, 53.3% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?

options.why: That is the molecular formula; reduce to the simplest ratio.
Correct. Convert each percent (in 100 g) to moles and divide by the smallest.

questions.explanation: The mole ratio reduces to CH2O; the molecular formula is C6H12O6.

questions.stem: At 298 K, ΔG° for a reaction is -16 kJ/mol. What is K?

options.why: Correct. K = e^(−ΔG°/RT), with ΔG° in J/mol and R = 8.314.

questions.explanation: ln K = 6.46; K = 638. Negative ΔG°: K greater than 1.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$, initial [H₂] = 1.4 M and [I₂] = 1.6 M, with no HI. At equilibrium, [HI] = 1.12 M. What is K?
For a reaction, ΔH° = 182 kJ/mol and ΔS° = -199 J/(mol·K). What is ΔG° at 528 K, and is the reaction favorable?

options.why: Correct. ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, with ΔS in kJ/(mol·K).
Convert ΔS from J to kJ.

questions.stem: What is the rate law?

options.why: Compare trials where only one concentration changes.
Correct. Doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 4; doubling [B] multiplies it by 2.
Orders are found from the data, not from coefficients.
Recheck how the rate changes when [B] doubles.

questions.explanation: Trials 1→2: rate ×4, so order 2 in A. Trials 1→3: rate ×2, so order 1 in B.

questions.stem: A photoelectron spectrum shows 5 peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative heights are 2 : 2 : 6 : 2 : 2. Which element is it?

options.why: Correct. The peaks correspond to $$1s^{2}\,2s^{2}\,2p^{6}\,3s^{2}\,3p^{2}$$, which has 14 electrons.

questions.stem: At 298 K, ΔG° for a reaction is -14 kJ/mol. What is K?

options.why: Correct. K = e^(−ΔG°/RT), with ΔG° in J/mol and R = 8.314.

questions.explanation: ln K = 5.65; K = 284. Negative ΔG°: K greater than 1.

questions.stem: For $$\ce{4Fe + 3O2 -> 2Fe2O3}$$, 30 g of $$\ce{Fe}$$ reacts with 92 g of $$\ce{O2}$$. What mass of $$\ce{Fe2O3}$$ can form?

options.why: Apply the mole ratio from the equation.
Correct. Fe is the limiting reactant.
Not all of both reactants reacts.
Use the limiting reactant, which gives less product.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.2 M solution of acetic acid (Ka = 1.8 \times 10^{-5})?

options.why: A weak acid does not ionize completely.
Correct. Solve Ka = x²/(C − x) for x = [H₃O⁺].

parts.prompt: Calculate the number of moles of CO₂ produced.

rubric.criterion: Correct moles using molar mass 100.09 g/mol and the 1:1 ratio.

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of CO₂ expected.
The student measures 2.127 L of gas. Calculate the percent yield, and give one experimental reason the yield could be less than 100%.

rubric.example: Incomplete decomposition (not heated long enough) or gas leaking from the apparatus.

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a complete Lewis diagram for CO₂, and identify its molecular geometry and the hybridization of carbon.

rubric.example: O=C=O with two lone pairs on each O (16 valence electrons).

parts.prompt: Explain why CO₂ is nonpolar even though C=O bonds are polar.

rubric.criterion: Linear symmetry makes the bond dipoles cancel.

parts.prompt: CaO is an ionic solid. Explain, using Coulomb's law, why CaO has a higher melting point than KCl.

rubric.criterion: Larger ion charges in CaO (2+/2−) than in KCl (1+/1−).
Greater electrostatic attraction (and smaller ions) means more energy is needed to separate the ions.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average rate of disappearance of X between 0 and 20 s.
Determine the order of the reaction with respect to X. Justify your answer using the data.

rubric.example: Equal time intervals give equal changes in ln[X].

parts.prompt: Write the rate law and determine the rate constant, with units.
Calculate the half-life of the reaction (for the initial concentration).
A proposed mechanism has a slow first step: X → Y + Z. Is the mechanism consistent with the rate law? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Yes; the slow step's elementary rate law matches the observed rate law.

parts.prompt: A catalyst is added. Explain its effect on the rate and on the rate constant, using activation energy.

rubric.example: The catalyst provides a new pathway.

rubric.criterion: Lower activation energy means a larger fraction of collisions are successful.

parts.prompt: Write the net ionic equation for the titration reaction.
Calculate the initial pH of the acid solution.

rubric.criterion: Ka expression set up with x = [H₃O⁺].

parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of NaOH needed to reach the equivalence point.
What is the pH at the half-equivalence point? Justify.
Calculate the pH at the equivalence point.

rubric.criterion: Uses Kb = Kw/Ka and the diluted [A⁻].

parts.prompt: Choose an appropriate indicator from: methyl orange (pKa 3.7), bromothymol blue (pKa 7.0), phenolphthalein (pKa 9.3). Justify.

rubric.criterion: Indicator whose pKa is closest to the equivalence pH.

parts.prompt: Explain why the solution at the half-equivalence point resists pH change when a small amount of HCl is added.

rubric.criterion: A⁻ reacts with added H⁺ to form HA (buffer).
rubric.example: A⁻ + H₃O⁺ → HA + H₂O, so the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes only slightly.

parts.prompt: Is the dissolution endothermic or exothermic? Justify.

rubric.example: Endothermic: the solution cooled, so energy was absorbed.

parts.prompt: Calculate the heat absorbed or released by the solution.
Calculate ΔH of dissolution in kJ/mol.
If some heat escaped to the surroundings, would the magnitude of the calculated ΔH be too large or too small? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Too small, because the measured temperature change is smaller than the true change.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced net ionic equation for the cell reaction.
Calculate E°cell.
Calculate ΔG° for the cell reaction.
The concentration of Zn²⁺ is increased to 2.0 M. Predict the effect on the cell potential and justify.

rubric.criterion: E decreases because Q increases (a product's concentration rises).
rubric.example: Q greater than 1 → E less than E°.

questions.title: Solubility of a slightly soluble salt

parts.prompt: Write the Ksp expression.
Calculate the molar solubility in pure water.
Calculate the molar solubility in a solution containing 0.1 M OH⁻ (from a soluble salt).
Explain how lowering the pH affects the solubility.

rubric.criterion: Correct reasoning about whether the anion is basic.
rubric.example: Solubility increases: H⁺ reacts with OH⁻ (a base), shifting the equilibrium toward dissolving.

parts.prompt: Write the electron configuration of Al.
Explain why the 1s peak of Al has a higher binding energy than the 1s peak of Mg.

rubric.criterion: Al has more protons, so 1s electrons are attracted more strongly (Coulomb's law).

parts.prompt: Describe one difference in the number or relative height of peaks between the two spectra.

rubric.criterion: A valid difference based on configurations.
rubric.example: Al has one more electron, so its outermost peak is taller or an extra peak appears.

parts.prompt: Which element has the larger atomic radius? Justify using Coulomb's law.

rubric.criterion: Mg: fewer protons with similar shielding, so valence electrons are held less tightly.
rubric.example: Same period; effective nuclear charge increases across.
